descriptor.assumptions: Assumes gel mole fractions approximate the batched Si/Al and that Al is the dominant trivalent framework heteroatom; gels using B, Ga, or Be for charge balance (for which this ratio overestimates charge demand) or postsynthesis-treated records will be misdescribed. The +1e-6 offset makes the ratio finite for Al-free gels, mapping them to a large value that the tree can use as an 'all-silica regime' split. The log scale is monotone, so it only reshapes the split thresholds, not the ordering. Assumes crystallized framework Si/Al correlates with, but need not equal, gel Si/Al.
descriptor.expected_effect: As log(Si/Al) increases, probability mass should shift from low-silica, inorganic-cation-templated frameworks (FAU, LTA, LEV) toward OSDA-templated and all-silica phases (MFI, MTW, *BEA, AFI). At the extreme Al-free end (log ratio ~6 when Al = 0), outcomes should be dominated by all-silica phases or Failed, since framework formation then relies on fluoride/defect charge compensation rather than Al.
descriptor.falsification: If the held-out publications show that product framework is essentially independent of the gel Si/Al ratio within fixed OSDA/alkali/fluoride regimes — e.g., the same topology obtained across several orders of magnitude of Si/(Al+1e-6) while different topologies appear at identical Si/Al with other variables changed — the descriptor adds no transferable information and its feature importance should be negligible. Also, if B- or Ga-substituted gels behave like Al gels at the same Si/Al, the Al-only normalization is an inadequate charge proxy.
descriptor.hypothesis: The gel Si/Al ratio is a primary control on which framework crystallizes: gels with abundant Al charge-compensated by inorganic cations crystallize low-silica frameworks, while Al-lean gels favor high-silica or all-silica phases whose void filling is dominated by the OSDA (or fluoride). Because the model only receives Si and Al as separate mole-fraction columns, a tree cannot split on their ratio; making the ratio (log-scaled for range compression) an explicit column lets single-split decisions separate the low- and high-silica synthesis regimes.
descriptor.mechanism: Framework Al generates one negative charge per T-site substitution that must be balanced by extraframework cations (Na+, K+, OSDA+). At low Si/Al the dense population of anionic sites requires small, hydrated inorganic cations and stabilizes open, low-silica topologies (e.g., FAU, LTA, gmelinic/LEV-type phases) whose cages accommodate hydrated cations. As Si/Al rises, fewer charge-compensating sites are needed and phase selection shifts to OSDA-templated or defect-charge-templated siliceous frameworks (e.g., MFI with TPA+, MTW with benzyltrimethylammonium, *BEA/BEC with TEA+, AFI/MTW all-silica in fluoride media). Literature [1] explicitly adjusts Si/Al so the SDA:Al ratio is ~1 for MTW crystallization; [2] shows OSDA-free *BEA formation is governed by the Na+-aluminosilicate gel Si/Al; [4] reports that at Si/Al = 20 the same SDA/alkali system switches phase selectivity (P1/SUZ-4 vs MOR); [3] shows Si/Al controls Al density and hence the host-guest charge ordering that directs a given framework.
descriptor.name: log_gel_SiAl_ratio

descriptor.assumptions: The formula assumes the recorded F mole fraction tracks free fluoride activity (ignoring protonation to HF, volatilization, and complexation by Al/B/Ge/Si), and that sda1 is the dominant organic cation (ignoring additional OSDAs or multivalent charges: osda_charge is not folded in, so monovalent OSDAs are implicitly assumed). It also ignores whether the gel is actually a fluoride route (OH-mediated gels with trace F contribute noise near the lower limit). The +1e-6 constants prevent division/log errors for gels without F or OSDA but compress the extreme ends of the range.
descriptor.expected_effect: As the descriptor increases from strongly negative to ~0 (F/OSDA from <<1 to ~1), Al-bearing phases (e.g. FER, MFI with Al) and amorphous outcomes should give way to OSDA/F-balanced phases such as *BEA; further increases into excess fluoride (>1) should favor cage-containing small-pore frameworks (LTA, CHA, AST-type) and reduce dense-phase/Failed outcomes in fluoride-rich gels.
descriptor.falsification: If, within this dataset, the product framework distribution is statistically invariant across the range of F/sda1 (e.g. the same frameworks dominate in both sub-stoichiometric and excess-fluoride gels, or the split on this column carries no information beyond F and sda1 individually), or if the observed phase ordering is inverted (excess fluoride consistently producing dense phases rather than cage-containing ones), the hypothesis is contradicted.
descriptor.hypothesis: The molar ratio of fluoride to organic structure-directing agent in the gel is a primary phase-selectivity switch in fluoride-mediated syntheses: near-stoichiometric F/OSDA (~1, the conventional fluoride route) favors one set of frameworks, sub-stoichiometric F/OSDA (<0.5) shifts selectivity toward frameworks that balance framework charge with heteroatoms (Al-containing phases, e.g. FER-type or MFI-type products), while excess fluoride (F/OSDA > 1) favors small-pore or cage-containing frameworks where F- is occluded in cages (LTA, AST, CHA-family) and can unlock otherwise inaccessible topologies. Since the classifier only receives F and sda1 as separate mole-fraction columns, a single tree split cannot access their ratio; making it an explicit log-scaled column lets one split separate the sub-stoichiometric, stoichiometric and excess-fluoride regimes.
descriptor.mechanism: In fluoride media the OSDA cation must be charge-balanced either by framework negative charges ([AlO4/2]- or [ZnO4/2]-, or connectivity defects) or by encapsulated F- in cages. When F is scarce relative to OSDA, framework defects/heteroatom incorporation must supply the compensating charge, biasing toward Al-bearing frameworks (or failure if no adequate balance is possible); when F is abundant, F- occlusion in small cages stabilizes frameworks with cage units and lowers crystallization driving force for dense phases. Evidence [2] shows pure-silica beta only at HF/OSDA = 1.00 while pure-silica ZSM-5 forms at HF/OSDA = 0.25 and amorphous at 0.13; evidence [3] shows ERS-7 forms only at HF/Ch+ = 2.0 whereas HF/Ch+ <= 1.0 yields FER/RUB-10, demonstrating F/OSDA-driven phase switches.

descriptor.assumptions: The mole-fraction ratio of H2O to the main T-atoms (Si, Ge, Al, P) is taken as a proxy for the classical H2O/SiO2 (or H2O/T-atom) gel concentration, ignoring the fact that mole fractions are normalized so the ratio is one minus the sum of all other species; it also assumes solvent-free and dry-gel-conversion recipes in the dataset are recorded consistently (their H2O fraction may reflect only added water, weakening the descriptor for those records). Ge and P are lumped with Si as framework-forming atoms, which is a simplification since Ge- and aluminophosphate chemistries have their own concentration effects. The log transform is purely for range compression across several orders of magnitude of dilution.
descriptor.expected_effect: As log_h2o_to_tatom_ratio increases (more dilute gels), high-framework-density and thermodynamically favored products (MTW, MOR, FER, dense/Failed outcomes, secondary phases from FAU gels such as sodalite/NaP-type) should become more likely, while metastable low-framework-density, cage-rich phases (*BEA/ISV/BEC, UTL, and generally large-cage fluoride-route phases) should become less likely and concentrate at the low end of the descriptor.
descriptor.falsification: If, after adding the column, split statistics show it carries negligible importance, or if the phases predicted to track dilution show no systematic ordering along the descriptor (e.g., *BEA equally likely at high and low water/T-atom ratios, or MTW favored in concentrated gels), the hypothesis is contradicted.
descriptor.hypothesis: The water-to-framework-forming-atom ratio (gel dilution) is an independent phase-selectivity lever that the current feature set cannot access: trees receive H2O, Si, Ge, Al and P only as separate normalized mole-fraction columns, and no single-column split can represent their ratio. Gels with low water/T-atom ratios (concentrated, high-supersaturation media) should preferentially crystallize metastable, low-framework-density, open frameworks whose formation needs fast nucleation, while dilute gels should favor thermodynamically more stable, higher-framework-density phases or denser/impurity products. This mirrors the previously added Si/Al and F/OSDA ratio descriptors but encodes a different, orthogonal axis of synthesis space.
descriptor.mechanism: Gel concentration controls supersaturation and thereby the nucleation-to-growth balance and the metastability window exploited during crystallization. In fluoride-mediated pure-silica systems it has been explicitly shown that the same OSDA yields the metastable open framework (*BEA) only in concentrated (low H2O/SiO2) gels, whereas more dilute mixtures, higher temperature and longer times give the denser, thermodynamically more stable phase (MTW/ZSM-12), with slow Ostwald ripening from Beta toward the denser phase [10]. Low water content also limits dissolution of soluble silicate/germanate species and favors occlusion of fluoride/OSDA in cages, stabilizing cage-containing low-density frameworks; high water content increases solubility and allows dissolution-recrystallization pathways that select equilibrium-like dense phases and secondary dense phases (e.g., NaP appearing from FAU gels as conditions push the system toward the stable phase [7]).
